summary: The recorded base reproducibly lets the server default reasoning_effort override both supported request forms at the actual chat-template render boundary. The exact candidate preserves whether the request supplied an effort before normalization and skips only the conflicting server default. Its regression tests, the full serving-chat unit file, and six independent precedence/boundary cases pass. This is a source fix plus regression hardening, not test-only hardening.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression file executed against untouched base source: nested and top-level explicit xhigh both rendered as medium (2 failed), while the silent-request default case passed.
Exact candidate at the chat-template render boundary: both request forms beat medium and a silent request receives medium (3 passed).
Full serving-chat unit suite on exact candidate: 138 passed and 68 subtests passed.

tests.command: Independent Python render-boundary probe recorded in raw/candidate-adversarial.log
tests.what_was_measured: Six cases: nested none, nested numeric 0.0, top-level max, silent request default, preservation of unrelated request kwargs/defaults, and conflicting request locations (nested request value retains existing precedence).
Confirmed tests imported /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py rather than an installed copy.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU kernels or model serving were needed or executed for this deterministic Python merge/render-boundary defect. The assigned device was detected as one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; this does not reproduce the report's 2x NVIDIA H200/CUDA/Qwen3.8 deployment.

remaining_limitations: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 weights were not available, so no full-model semantic or reasoning-length comparison was run.

The prepared environment has one AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 with ROCm 7.2, whereas the report used two NVIDIA H200 NVL GPUs with CUDA 13.0 and TP/EP=2; distributed and architecture-specific behavior remains untested.
No native files changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was neither applicable nor performed.
The verification establishes request/default precedence through the real conversion and tokenizer apply_chat_template boundary; it does not claim model-output quality or reasoning-length equivalence.
